Led by Dr. Michelle Oblak, Animal Health Partners Research Chair in Veterinary Medical Innovation, the research team is evaluating the use of nanoparticles and laser light therapy as a non-surgical treatment approach for cats diagnosed with oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC). About OCSCC OCSCC is a relatively common and aggressive type of oral cancer in cats. It typically originates in the tissues of the mouth, including the gums, tongue and palate and presents as an ulcerative lesion that can cause drooling, bad breath and difficulty eating. Profile Samuel David Stewart Studies Ethos Precision Medicine Umbrella Study for Hemangiosarcoma (Ethos-PUSH) Ethos-PUSH: Hemangiosarcoma Ethos Precision Medicine Umbrella Study for Hemangiosarcoma (Ethos-PUSH) Ethos-PUSH: Hemangiosarcoma Canine splenic hemangiosarcoma is an aggressive cancer with limited treatment options available. Dogs presenting with this disease often have spontaneous internal bleeding that results in sudden onset of weakness or collapse. Although this is a common consequence for hemangiosarcoma, any other tumor of the spleen can spontaneously bleed resulting in these same changes. Dogs who have a bleeding splenic tumor must undergo surgery to remove the spleen (called splenectomy). This procedure both removes the source of life-threatening hemorrhage and provides tissue samples for making a final diagnosis. Roughly 40% of dogs have benign splenic disease causing the internal bleeding and will be cured with surgery alone. Many of the remaining dogs will have hemangiosarcoma as the cause of their bleeding and will require chemotherapy following surgery to delay or prevent metastatic disease. The use of either doxorubicin or carboplatin alone as a treatment for hemangiosarcoma has been studied, and studies with propranolol (historically used to treat heart disease) have shown promise as an added treatment against hemangiosarcoma, however, survival times still remain quite low. We are hopeful that survival times can be further improved using a combination approach to treatment, with combination of both intravenous and oral treatments. Dogs with hemangiosarcoma of the spleen, liver, heart or intramuscular region will be considered for inclusion in this study.
